spec_atomic_units: Module has a synchronous active-high reset input `reset`
Output `q[3:0]` represents the current count value, ranging from 0 (0000) to 9 (1001) in binary representation
If the `reset` input is asserted (high), the output `q[3:0]` is forced to 0 (0000)
Reset is synchronous, meaning it takes effect on the active edge of the clock signal
If the `reset` input is not asserted (low), the current value of `q[3:0]` is examined
If `q[3:0]` is less than 9 (1001), the output `q[3:0]` is incremented by 1
If `q[3:0]` is equal to 9 (1001), the output `q[3:0]` is set to 0 (0000), completing the decade count sequence
Output `q` changes only on the rising edge of `clk`
When `reset` is high, `q` becomes 0 on the next rising edge of `clk`
When `reset` is low, `q` increments by 1 on each rising edge of `clk` until it reaches 9
When `q` is 9 and `reset` is low, `q` becomes 0 on the next rising edge of `clk`
The design uses a single register `q` declared as `output reg [3:0] q`
The register is updated inside an `always @(posedge clk)` block, indicating that the updates are synchronous and occur on the rising edge of the clock
The updates to `q` are performed using non-blocking assignments (`<=`)
The counter resets to 0 when `reset` is high
When `reset` is low, the counter increments until it reaches 9, at which point it resets to 0
The counter has a period of 10 clock cycles
